bias: 'Two days of failed auctions, developing P-shaped profiles, and the potential for a major directional resolution.' CPI Tuesday was volatile and two-sided: sellers had a favorable chance to reverse Monday's recovery and liquidated hard intraday, but neither ES nor NQ took out Monday's low — and buyers haven't finished the job either (NQ twice failed to reclaim the upper boundary of its developing balance). Both weekly profiles are P-shaped (forced buying / short covering, then consolidation): the body of the P is a balance to rotate within; an upside break with acceptance starts a fresh distribution higher; a downside failure — acceptance below the body, then defended as resistance — risks liquidation down the thin stem. 'Neither side has finished the job.' Favor treating the body as a balance while staying prepared for the resolution.
wildcard: Distinguish a brief excursion outside the balance from genuine acceptance — don't blindly trade every boundary break; a failed break is an excellent trade the other way. NQ: buyers reclaimed and defended the lower HTF inflection area but struggle beneath the next; developing supply 27910-27950 (already tested after hours to 27916). ES: the late rally carried price well above Tuesday's value area ('made little sense'); Tuesday's VAH sits effectively at 7539-7543; 7558-7566 (Oct low 7558 + the 7562-7563 daily) may be developing into an important decision area. Veterans Day (bond market closed). Daily: ES 7662, 7631-7634, 7562-7563, 7454-7458, 7412-7415; NQ 27869, 27689, 27110-27123, 27057.

brief.higher: Buyers defending the lower boundary and eventually accepting above the upper boundary (Monday's high / Thursday's open and high, 200-day above) → the higher inflection areas from the weekly: 28200-28233, 28443-28485.
brief.lower: Acceptance below the body, defended as resistance → liquidation down the stem — but 27425-27458 (Friday's high) and 27313-27339 (Monday's open/low) are significant responsive-buying areas sellers must overcome first.
